An All Progressives Congress chieftain in Edo State, Julius Olele, has identified improved security, infrastructure development and the restoration of public confidence as major achievements of Governor Monday Okpebholo’s administration ahead of his second anniversary. Olele, a member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Edo State, said the governor had demonstrated commitment to addressing the challenges confronting residents through investments in road construction, stronger collaboration with security agencies and closer monitoring of government projects. Okpebholo will mark two years in office on Thursday, November 12, having been sworn in as governor alongside his deputy, Dennis Idahosa, on November 12, 2024. Speaking in an interview with The PUNCH ahead of the anniversary, Olele said the administration had made security a priority following concerns over kidnapping, cult-related violence and other criminal activities that had affected residents, businesses and movement across the state. “Before this administration came into office, kidnapping, cult-related violence and other criminal activities had become major concerns for residents. These problems affected businesses, restricted movement and discouraged many Edo indigenes in the diaspora from returning home. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Governor Monday Okpebholo has made security a major priority through stronger collaboration with security agencies, community-based security initiatives and tougher measures against criminal activities. “While security remains an ongoing responsibility, there is a renewed determination to make Edo safer for everyone,” he said. On infrastructure, the APC chieftain commended the administration’s road construction and rehabilitation projects across the state, particularly the Ramat Park and Adesuwa flyovers in Benin City. Olele described the restoration of public confidence as another significant achievement, arguing that residents wanted a government that was visible, accessible and committed to delivering results. On the impact of the administration’s policies on residents, Olele said improved confidence in personal safety and efforts to tackle criminal activities were among the important developments since the governor assumed office. Identifying unfinished road projects as one of the administration’s major outstanding responsibilities, Olele said the government must sustain the pace of construction and ensure quality delivery. He acknowledged that the rainy season had presented some challenges to construction activities but expressed optimism that contractors would maintain progress. Olele urged residents to give the administration more time, arguing that its achievements within two years offered prospects for greater development if the momentum was sustained. Adeyinka Adedipe
